body:
MYK (2026-07-27, chat), riffing forward from T118's ruling: "in addition to promotion a
user's container could be *ejected* and used to bootstrap a new store of which they are the
operator." It is a natural extension, and most of it already exists.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is assembly rather than invention:
- A container mount already serves `/<container>/federate`, which answers its own raw signed deltas.
  That IS the export.
- `loam init --seed <hex>` stands up a home with a chosen operator identity.
- `loam pull <file|url>` lands an offer into it.
- The three composed were REHEARSED on 2026-07-27 for the board store's move to ~/.loam: same
  operator, 118 deltas, the app serving from the new store. Ejection is that rehearsal with a
  DIFFERENT operator at the far end.
- `loam.container.detached` (§27) is already the operator's record that a separate container's store
  is deliberately gone. Ejection wants that record, plus what the ejected store carries away.

WHAT DOES NOT FALL OUT FREE — four things, and the first two need Myk's word.

(1) WHO HOLDS THE CONTAINER'S OPERATOR SEED. This is the load-bearing question, and it decides
whether ejection means anything. If the HOST holds it, then ejection hands over a key the host still
has a copy of, and the user is never the sole operator of anything. If the USER holds it from the
start, ejection is real — and the host then CANNOT sign inside the user's container, which is
consistent with §28 rather than a problem: the host's seeding deltas arrive authored by the host and
are inert until the container's operator blesses them, exactly as foreign law should be. RECOMMEND:
the user holds it. The operator provisions the ACCOUNT; the account's container mints its own key.
That also makes T118's model sharper — the operator cannot forge the user's writes.

(2) WHAT EJECTION DISCLOSES. The container holds what the user wrote PLUS what the membership rule
seeded in. So ejection carries away exactly the container's membership, no more — a clean sentence,
and worth stating in the spec as the promise rather than leaving a reader to infer it. Myk should
confirm that is the intended reach, because it is the sentence a tenant will quote.

(3) THE ERASURE OBLIGATION, and this one is an H7 trap waiting to be built. Once a container can be
ejected, the operator can no longer erase from it — the ejected store is a NEW PEER, and §29's
receipt already says peers are not reached. So the moment ejection ships, every erasure report must
NAME ejected containers as a surface it cannot reach, or the report overclaims. This is the same
class as the credentials.json disclosure added on 2026-07-27, and the same fix shape: the
`nonClaim` list and `UNSWEPT_SURFACES` grow one entry. Do it IN the ejection PR, not after.

(4) THE EJECTED STORE'S GENESIS. A store has a genesis assembled for its operator. The ejected
deltas include host-authored ones from the seeding edge, whose author is a stranger to the new
store. §28's inert-until-blessed rule means they carry no force there until the new operator adopts
them by §24.3 — which is correct, and is the same promotion mechanism running one level out. Worth a
rail rather than a comment: a host-authored declaration in an ejected store binds NOTHING until the
new operator adopts it.

WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING BEYOND ELEGANCE: it is a real answer to lock-in, and it is the same
machinery as federation rather than a new subsystem. "Your container can leave, and it becomes yours"
is a promise very few systems can make, and Loam can make it because the deltas were always signed
and content-addressed.

RAILS, both sides: an ejected store answers the user's own claims through a reading AND a
host-authored declaration in it binds nothing until adopted. Plus the erasure half, two-sided: a
receipt issued after an ejection NAMES the ejected container as unreachable, and still proves what it
CAN prove about the ground it kept.

DEPENDS ON T118 — there is nothing to eject until a user's container is a real scope with its own
operator. Design-stage: it decides what the system promises about data leaving, so the spec section
is Myk's merge.
title: Ejection — a user's container leaves and becomes a store they are the operator of
